articles.title: Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows
articles.summary: Global carbon emissions are expected to fall slightly in 2026, but not because of major progress on climate action. Instead, it's high energy prices following the US attack on Iran that's driving the…

image.caption: Carbon emissions are the main drivers of climate changeImage: Jason Whitman/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.
"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons."
The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.
No structural change yet

The study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.
"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.
Turkey on the climate frontline

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterwards, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%."
Emissions expected to rebound

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind, the temporary emissions reversal, there's also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.
"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

articles.title: Escudero hopes Sara Duterte impeachment trial over before Christmas
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero expressed hope Tuesday that the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte will be finished before Christmas or New Year.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 11:54am
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero expressed hope Tuesday that the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte will be finished before Christmas or New Year.

Escudero, however, clarified that the impeachment court is not following any timeline and could not say exactly when the trial would end as it would depend on the evidence presented by the defense and the flow of the hearings.

“Sa akin mismo, kung ako ang tatanungin syempre in a perfect world, sana matapos ang impeachment sinuman ang matalo o manalo bago mag-Pasko, bago mag-New Year para may bago tayong yugto na namang haharapin sa bagong taon, hindi ‘yung babalikan na naman natin ito sa darating na bagong taon ng 2027,” he said in an ambush interview.

(Personally, if you ask me, in a perfect world, I would hope that the impeachment concludes before Christmas or the New Year, regardless of who wins or loses. This way, we can face a new chapter in the coming year, rather than having to revisit this same issue when 2027 comes.)
“Whichever side prevails, sana ito ay malampasan at matapos natin ngayong taong ito para may bagong mga hamon at problema na naman tayong haharapin sa darating na taon,” he added.
(Whichever side prevails, I hope we can move past this and bring it to a close within this year, so that we may face new challenges and problems in the year ahead.)

The defense is currently presenting evidence and witnesses for Article II of the impeachment case against Duterte alleging her unexplained wealth due to supposed failure to truthfully disclose assets in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN) and failure to divest in businesses as required for the President and Vice President under a Constitutional provision.
The prosecution previously dropped three out of the four Articles of Impeachment leveled against the Vice President, saying its case would stand on Article II alone.

The withdrawn impeachment articles were: Article I on confidential funds; Article III on bribery; and Article IV on assassination plot, grave threats, and inciting to sedition against President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and former Speaker and incumbent Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Post falsely claims ICC junked Duterte case over ‘fabricated’ evidence
articles.summary: The ICC confirmed all charges in April, with the trial set to begin on November 30

blocks.text: Claim: Three International Criminal Court (ICC) judges dismissed the crimes against humanity case against former president Rodrigo Duterte due to fabricated evidence by former senator Antonio Trillanes IV.

Why we fact-checked this: A video posted on October 30 by the Facebook page Noel Weng Acido carries a thumbnail with partly obscured text that appears to read, “ICC case dismissed” and “Ebidensya ni (evidence of) Trillanes.”
The caption claims, “Hindi yan fake news, tatlong ICC judges pina-dismiss ang kaso ni PRRD dahil ebidensya ni [Trillanes] ay gawa-gawa lang, laya na si PRRD.”
(That’s not fake news, three ICC judges dismissed [former president Rodrigo Roa Duterte]’s case because Trillanes’ evidence was fabricated. PRRD is free now.)
The narration repeats the claim: “Breaking news, 3 judges sa ICC pina-dismiss ang kaso ni PRRD dahil ‘yong mga ebidensya ay gawa-gawa lang ni Trillanes.”
(Breaking news, three ICC judges dismissed PRRD’s case because the evidence was fabricated by Trillanes.)
As of writing, the video had 182,000 views, 2,700 reactions, 197 comments, and 419 shares.
The facts: There is no ICC ruling, statement, or credible report saying the case has been dismissed. In fact, it has moved to trial.

Two groups of three ICC judges have handled the former president’s case, and neither has dismissed it. The first, Pre-Trial Chamber I, heard oral submissions by the prosecution and defense in February and confirmed all charges in April. The pre-trial chamber was composed of judges Iulia Antoanella Motoc, Reine Adélaïde Sophie Alapini-Gansou, and María del Socorro Flores Liera.

The case is now assigned to Trial Chamber III, which will begin proceedings on November 30. The chamber is composed of judges Joanna Korner from the UK, Keebong Paek from South Korea, and Nicolas Guillou from France. None served on the first panel, as ICC rules require. On October 8, judges also ruled that Duterte was fit to stand trial.
​​Duterte is facing three counts of crimes against humanity due to his alleged involvement in the killings under his war on drugs and the Davao Death Squad.

Trillanes’ role: Trillanes, a fierce critic of the former president, has played an active role in the drug war case. In June 2017, he and then-Magdalo party-list Representative Gary Alejano filed a 45-page submission asking the ICC to investigate Duterte’s drug war. It followed an earlier complaint filed by lawyer Jude Sabio accusing Duterte of mass murder in the Philippines.

The submission cited accounts from self-confessed hitman Edgar Matobato, retired police officer Arturo Lascañas, and a police officer identified as PO1 Tacorda, in which they described planned killings linked to police operations. (READ: What neutralization means in Duterte’s drug war, according to sources)

During the confirmation of charges hearing in February 2026, prosecutors presented witness statements, documents, and Duterte’s own public remarks that they said showed the alleged policy of widespread killings under the former strongman.

In confirming the charges against Duterte, the ICC judges said there were “substantial grounds” to believe that Duterte was criminally responsible for the crimes charged. Contrary to the claim, there were no mentions of any supposed fabrication of evidence allegedly by Trillanes or anyone else.

In February, Trillanes was accused of receiving bribes to facilitate the ICC investigation into the Duterte drug war. The former lawmaker denied the claim, saying it was an attempt to discredit the tribunal’s proceedings.

Road to trial: Duterte has been in ICC custody since March 2025. If convicted, he could face a prison sentence of up to 30 years or life imprisonment. His case could last several years, with ICC-accredited assistant to counsel Kristina Conti earlier saying previous trials have lasted around three years, with some taking as long as a decade. (READ: Where are we now in Rodrigo Duterte’s ICC case?) – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

articles.title: California voters reject proposed billionaire tax
articles.summary: California voters have rejected a proposed one-time tax on the net worth of billionaires in the state following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders…

image.caption: A sign is displayed at the Billionaire Tax Now booth at the 2026 California Democratic Party State Convention in San Francisco in February 2026. California voters have since rejected a tax on the net worth of billionaires. (Jeff Chiu/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New

California voters have rejected a proposed one-time tax on the net worth of billionaires in the state following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop their taxes from going up. one-time tax on state billionaires' fortunes
Critics said one-time tax on state billionaires' fortunes would prompt ultrawealthy taxpayers to leave state

California voters have rejected a proposed tax on the net worth of billionaires following a contentious ballot fight that generated huge spending by some prominent tech leaders eager to stop their taxes from going up.

The measure's failure is a win for Democratic leaders who opposed it, including Gov. Gavin Newsom, who's deciding whether to run for president in 2028. Critics of the tax, known as Proposition 40, said it would have prompted ultrawealthy taxpayers to leave the state.
The "no" side raised roughly 10 times as much as the "yes" side. Google co-founder Sergey Brin alone dumped more than $100 million US into a political action committee working to defeat the measure.
The measure would have imposed a one-time five per cent tax on the wealth of Californians whose net worth exceeds $1 billion US. It would have been the first of its kind in the U.S.

Most of the money would have been used to backfill federal funding cuts to health care, and 10 per cent would have gone toward education and food-assistance programs. SEIU United Healthcare Workers West, California's health-care union, said the tax was necessary to replace an estimated $100 billion US the state will lose in federal health-care funding over five years.
Long championed by progressives

Proposition 40 was the nation's biggest test yet on an idea progressives have long championed: raising taxes on the ultra-rich by targeting the main way they make their money — through their investments as opposed to their work paycheques.

The measure attracted support from liberal leaders beyond the state, including Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders, who rallied in cities across California in the race's closing weeks to urge voters to pass it.

The measure attracted support from liberal leaders beyond the state, including Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders — seen speaking at a Ballots Over Billionaires rally in Los Angeles last month. (Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)

Billionaires donated millions of dollars to a political action committee, Building a Better California, working to defeat the measure. The committee, which backed other measures on the ballot designed to nullify the tax, raised more than $333 million US, nearly a third of which came from Brin.

Brin, along with his fellow Google co-founder Larry Page, was among the billionaires who started cutting ties with the state in anticipation of the possible tax. Another tech mogul, Facebook co-founder Mark Zuckerberg, said he would remain in the state for eight years and made a deal with Meta to help him pay the tax without losing his ownership stake in the company.
Opposed by some Democratic allies

Some traditional Democratic allies, including Planned Parenthood and the California Medical Association, were part of a coalition opposing the measure. They were concerned about how the tax revenue would be divvied up and about the potential impact on the state's budget if there was a mass exodus of wealthy taxpayers.
California's budget relies heavily on the income tax of the state's richest residents.
"Proposition 40 was a reckless experiment conducted on our state's economy with little regard for the harms it would cause," the coalition said in a statement.
Robert Swonger, an auto glass technician living near Sacramento who is politically independent, said before voting concluded on Nov. 3 that he planned to vote against it.
"Obviously, I would like billionaires not to have as much money as they do," he said. "But I don't believe taxing them out of existence is going to work."

California Gov. Gavin Newsom opposed Proposition 40. He says a California wealth tax would disadvantage the state, but he supports a national minimum tax on anyone with a net worth above $100 million US. (Jill Connelly/The Associated Press)
Tax would disadvantage state: Newsom

Progressive politicians, including Sanders and Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren, have long supported a federal wealth tax. Newsom says a California wealth tax would disadvantage the state, but he supports a national minimum tax on anyone with a net worth above $100 million US.

Days before Sanders held rallies in California cities last month, Newsom told reporters that the senator's focus on wealth inequality was "spot-on." But he said that "on this issue, we fundamentally disagree."

Supporters of the California tax started running ads recently in New Hampshire, New Mexico and Virginia, states that will vote early in the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, that criticize Newsom for his opposition to the measure.

articles.title: Marcos to newly appointed AFP officials: Never lose trust, confidence of Filipinos
articles.summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Tuesday urged newly promoted generals and flag officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to never lose the "trust and confidence" of Filipinos…

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 11:41am

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Tuesday urged newly promoted generals and flag officers of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) to never lose the "trust and confidence" of Filipinos as they take their oaths of office.
"No matter how advanced our capabilities may become, we must never lose sight of the trust and confidence of the Filipino people," Marcos said during his speech.
"Sustaining that trust is a responsibility that all of us share, government, our institutions, and our communities," he added.
Marcos made the statement as he said, "a modern military requires leaders who serve with competence, integrity, and accountability."
He also committed that the government will provide the support needed by the AFP to perform its mandate.
General Antonio Nafarrete took his oath as AFP chief of staff along with 33 other newly promoted generals and flag officers of the AFP.
In August, the Commission on Appointments confirmed the appointments and nomination of Nafarrete and 37 other generals, flag and senior officers.

Suceeding General Romeo Brawner Jr., Nafarrete previously headed the Western Mindanao Command (WestMinCom), where he oversaw joint military operations against communist insurgents and local terrorist groups.

He also commanded the 1st Infantry Division, Joint Task Force Zampelan, and held leadership posts in the 11th Infantry Division, the 1101st Infantry Brigade, and the AFP's operations staff (J3). — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Bring the heat: K/DA burning walls between gaming and pop culture
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – For the third time since its debut back at the 2018 Worlds in Incheon, South Korea, and the ALL OUT release back in 2020, Riot Games’ virtual K-pop group K/DA returned once…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – For the third time since its debut back at the 2018 Worlds in Incheon, South Korea, and the ALL OUT release back in 2020, Riot Games’ virtual K-pop group K/DA returned once again with another banger titled ‘FIRESTARTER’.

Within two weeks since its release, the whole EP hit #1 on the worldwide iTunes Album Chart, enter the YouTube global weekly chart at #9, and peak at #87 on the global Top 200 list chart for Billboard. It also became the highest-charting song from Riot Games on the global Spotify chart.
Feeling the heat

The K/DA craze didn’t just reflect on numerous music charts. From people vibing to the beats to the jaw-dropping dance covers, the reception for K/DA has been lit all over the internet, especially for Akali and Ahri’s artists, Jeon Soyeon and Cho Miyeon of the K-pop group i-dle. Even fans of the P-pop group SB19 are awaiting the group’s official cover of FIRESTARTER on November 10.
The beloved group captured hearts and ears from all over the world, including people who haven’t played League of Legends and casual music listeners.
Riot Games and League of Legends: Wild Rift recently celebrated this latest K/DA release with the “FIRE IT UP: The K/DA Comeback Party.”
People across different games and ages enjoyed vibing to the music of the Riot Games music universe, as most of the attendees dressed up to their favorite characters.
Some of the attendees were also lucky to participate in a live game of AAA ARAM, featuring its newest augments inspired by HEARTSTEEL, Pentakill, and TRUE DAMAGE.
RELATED STORY: Overwatch launches Midseason 5 update with new events, skins

Additional details for the exclusive, K/DA-inspired skinline for Wild Rift called HEATBRINGER were also showcased at the listening party. It will feature WR-locked game cosmetics for Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai’ Sa, as well as the grand and highly sought-after Prestige K/DA HEATBRINGER Evelynn.

For Coleen Ramos, APAC Publishing Manager for League of Legends: Wild Rift, celebrations like the listening party can be like embers—a glowing reminder of how music and gaming culture burn brightly over time.
“I think Riot does really well in terms of going beyond and exploring music and also TV series, right? Like Arcane.”

“As I mentioned, as a player, I would like to see not the usual kind of events where people just talk about the game. When we’re planning this, it’s really more about engagement. And because it doesn’t happen often, it does have that effect that people want to go to it as soon as possible,” Ramos shared.
Considering that there were requests for another listening party sent to them, Ramos assured, “If there’s going to be another big music moment, then we already know we need a bigger venue than this.”

articles.title: One Nation dumps Victorian election candidate who praised Adolf Hitler as ‘GOAT’
articles.summary:
Party disendorses Preston candidate Franco Guardiani after social media posts emerge

One Nation Victoria has disendorsed a candidate whose private social media account described Adolf Hitler…

blocks.text: One Nation Victoria has disendorsed a candidate whose private social media account described Adolf Hitler as the “GOAT” and claimed that “importing Islam is making pedophilia legal”.
In a now deleted social media post, the party’s candidate for Preston, Franco Guardiani, commented on a social media post on X asking people to: “Describe Hitler in one word? Be brutally honest”.
Guardiani then replied with the acronym GOAT, which stands for greatest of all time.
The party was made aware of Guardiani’s social media posts on Tuesday morning and disendorsed him a short time later. A party official discussed the posts with Guardiani and confirmed they were real.
“At a time when Jewish Australians are experiencing unprecedented persecution, we are appalled that these comments have been made,” said the party’s Victorian leader, Warren Pickering.
“As soon as we became aware, we acted. Preston candidate Franco Guardiani is no longer part of our party.
“Anyone who holds such views is on notice: they do not have a place in One Nation.”
The former candidate’s X account contains several Islamophobic comments including references to bulldozing or setting fire to mosques.
The account has also engaged with posts by the anti-immigrant group Kights Templar International.

It is unclear how the candidate’s social media history was not detected during candidate selection and vetting processes. The party has claimed to have invested time and money into improving this process.
Guardiani is no longer listed as a One Nation candidate on the party’s official website.
Guardiani has been contacted for comment.

articles.title: [Rear View] What part of ‘I’m not running’ don’t you understand?
articles.summary: A real coalition should answer a question the pinks have rarely asked themselves: who can actually win? If the honest answer lies outside the tent, the tent needs to get bigger.

blocks.text: Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo could not have been clearer when she declared on Monday, November 9 — for the second time this year — that she will not run for president in 2028. “Matagal nang sarado,” she said, adding that nothing will change her mind.
The Liberal Party (LP) old guard heard her but remained unmoved.

Representative Leila de Lima, who chairs the LP, called Robredo the country’s “best hope” and said she refuses to believe the decision is final. Senator Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan resurrected the ghost of 2010, reminding all who cared to listen that the late former president Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino said the same thing. Pangilinan, Robredo’s running mate in 2022, has been warning since April that without Robredo, the opposition risks a leadership vacuum and a splintered coalition.

Meanwhile, supporters of Senator Risa Hontiveros and Senator Bam Aquino were back at each other’s throats online within hours, treating Robredo’s statement as the starting gun for a succession fight rather than a call for serious groundwork and coalition building.
I wrote in July that the pinks are their own worst enemies. Nothing since has changed my mind.
What is shaping up is a not-so-civil war, generational and ideological, within the pink movement.

In one corner is the LP establishment, the party of four presidents, which still believes the 2028 standard-bearer must come from its ranks or at least carry its blessing. In another is Akbayan, the civil-society, social-democratic upstart that topped the party list race in 2025 and has been aggressively running its Risa Na! campaign since June. And somewhere in between is Bam Aquino, who left the LP, nominally some would say, and whose supporters see in him a third Aquino presidency.
All three camps are after the same grail: Robredo’s anointment. There lies the problem.

The organized pinks carry the conceit that the choice must be theirs alone to make, that the unified candidate against “Dutertismo” can only come from inside their tent. The rest are unworthy and impure.
The surveys should give them a reality check. After Robredo, the strongest name against Vice President Sara Duterte is Senator Raffy Tulfo.

In a commissioned Pulse Asia head-to-head conducted in February and early March, Tulfo tied Duterte at 46%. In Pulse Asia’s September survey, Duterte beat Hontiveros 60 to 23. In the three-way races without Robredo, Tulfo still placed second, ahead of Hontiveros and narrowly ahead of Aquino.

A deep dive reveals the Tulfo advantage. In the March matchup, Tulfo led Duterte in the ABC class and is statistically tied in Class D, 47 to 48. Robredo’s edge over Duterte was confined to ABC; Duterte led her in D and E, or almost 90% of the electorate. The pinks may win the Makati and BGC crowd, but Tulfo competes in Cubao.

The strong brand recognition for Tulfo is built on decades of delivering quick justice through media. The Tulfo brothers deliver where government fails, berating on the air the abusive and the callous. It is empathy the masa can see and hear and cheer, even those light-hearted episodes featuring quarreling couples. The pink personalities offer competence and decency, and voters keep telling them that is not enough.
Like Robredo, Tulfo has said he will not run. The difference is that the LP keeps courting one and ignoring the other.

There is a larger point the pinks keep missing or ignoring. The enemy is not only Sara Duterte. It is “Dutertismo” — the nostalgia for the iron hand, the desensitization to killings, the smart-shaming that has turned kabobohan into a badge of authenticity.

Whatever the impeachment court decides, Dutertismo remains, along with a bench of heirs eager to inherit the base, namely Mayor Baste Duterte, Senator Robin Padilla, and Senator Bong Go. A guilty verdict disqualifies the Vice President from holding public office, but she can still campaign for the Duterte candidate.
Jail her and the Marcos administration creates a martyr. Disqualify her and you have a fierce endorser eager to settle a score.

blocks.caption: [Rear View] The 2028 battle is with Dutertismo, not just Sara

blocks.text: “Dutertismo” is a populist movement, and populism has never been beaten by a lecture or an online essay. It is beaten by someone who can capture the protest vote before the Dutertes can consolidate it, and who can speak to Class D and E voters in a language they know and trust. None of the pink personalities has this to offer.

I am not saying that the pinks should surrender their values. My point is that they should stop treating the presidency as an heirloom to be passed down within the party or family. A real coalition should answer a question the pinks have rarely asked themselves: who can actually win? If the honest answer lies outside the tent, the tent needs to get bigger.

Until then, the LP will keep waiting for Leni, the Risa and Bam stans will keep fighting over an empty chair, and Sara Duterte, or the “Dutertismo” candidate, will keep harvesting converts. – Rappler.com
Joey Salgado is a former journalist, and a government and political communications practitioner. He served as spokesperson for former vice president Jejomar Binay.

articles.title: MVP’s Landco eyes 25-year Camp John Hay Golf lease
articles.summary: The BCDA is seeking at least P500 million in improvement works for the golf course under a proposed 25-year contract, with a possible 25-year extension

blocks.text: ICONIC. The John Hay Golf Course, set against Baguio’s lush pine forests, gears up to host the 75th Fil-Am Invitational Golf Tournament.
Mia Magdalena Fokno/Rappler
The BCDA is seeking at least P500 million in improvement works for the golf course under a proposed 25-year contract, with a possible 25-year extension

items: Landco Pacific Corporation is collaborating with Turfgrass Management Inc. and Golfplus Management Inc. to pursue a 25-year lease for the John Hay Golf Course in Camp John Hay.

The consortium plans to submit an unsolicited proposal to the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), which is seeking significant private investment for improvements to the golf course and hotels in the area.
Landco aims to restore the golf course while preserving its heritage, enhancing its hospitality operations, and providing more attractions for tourists in Baguio City.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

BAGUIO CITY, Philippines – Landco Pacific Corporation (Landco) is setting its sights on another major Camp John Hay property, joining forces with two golf management firms to pursue a lease of at least 25 years for the historic John Hay Golf Course.

The leisure real estate developer under the Manuel V. Pangilinan (MVP) Group announced on Sunday, November 8 that it had signed a memorandum of agreement with Turfgrass Management Inc. (TMI) and Golfplus Management Inc. (GMI) to jointly pursue the rehabilitation, development, operation, and maintenance of the course.

The three companies plan to submit an unsolicited proposal to the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), which regained control of Camp John Hay in January 2025 following its prolonged legal dispute with Camp John Hay Development Corporation (CJHDevCo).

Golfplus is already among the course’s interim operators, alongside DuckWorld Philippines, the public-facing name associated with Duck Sports and Music Productions Inc. BCDA extended their management arrangement through 2026 while preparing to select a long-term operator.

Landco also has an established presence in Camp John Hay. Through its hospitality arm, Landco Lifestyle Ventures (LLV), it currently manages John Hay Hotels, formerly The Manor and Forest Lodge, as well as the John Hay Convention Center.

blocks.caption: Why support sports? MVP’s story goes back to Baguio’s playgrounds

blocks.text: However, its hotel management arrangement is temporary. BCDA and its subsidiary, John Hay Management Corporation (JHMC), are also preparing to bid out the hotels’ long-term operations, with Landco expressing interest in participating.
The proposed golf course partnership comes as BCDA seeks substantial private investment to improve Camp John Hay’s recreational facilities.

In an October 16 media briefing, BCDA President and CEO Joshua Bingcang said the government was seeking at least P500 million in improvement works for the golf course under a proposed 25-year contract, with a possible 25-year extension.

The selected operator would be responsible for upgrading, maintaining, and managing the facility. BCDA is separately seeking at least P1 billion in investments for the two hotels, including refurbishment and additional rooms.
Landco’s announcement did not specify how much the consortium intends to invest, the extent of rehabilitation work, or when its proposal would be submitted.
It also raises a question about how an unsolicited proposal would be considered alongside BCDA’s previously announced competitive selection process.

As Rappler reported in June 2026, BCDA had targeted the third quarter of the year to begin bidding out the golf course’s long-term management. The agency confirmed that the incumbent operator would be eligible to participate.
By October, BCDA was targeting the fourth quarter for the bidding, indicating that the timetable had moved.
Landco president and CEO Erickson Y. Manzano said the partnership aims to restore the course while preserving its heritage for future generations.
“By partnering with experts who know this game and this terrain, we hope to restore the course with the care it deserves, for the next generation of players and visitors,” Manzano said.
He added that an improved golf course would complement Landco’s hospitality operations and give tourists another reason to extend their stay in Baguio.

The golf course, one of Camp John Hay’s best-known recreational landmarks, was opened to the general public following BCDA’s takeover in 2025. Its interim management arrangement was intended to keep the facility operating while the government prepared a longer-term agreement.

The proposed lease also comes amid Baguio City’s continuing efforts to secure compliance with the 19 conditionalities governing Camp John Hay’s development, including its share in revenues and lease rentals. During an October 19 city council session, the city treasurer placed the city’s outstanding claim at approximately P225 million.
For now, the agreement among Landco, TMI, and Golfplus establishes their intention to pursue the golf course concession, not an award from BCDA.
The agency has yet to announce a winning long-term operator, while Landco has not disclosed when its consortium will formally submit its proposal. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Tensions in the South China Sea persist as Beijing claims almost the entire strategic waterway, through which more than $3 trillion worth of goods are shipped annually.
The area is also subject to overlapping territorial and maritime claims by the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia.

The Philippine government uses the name West Philippine Sea to refer to maritime areas on the western side of the Philippine archipelago, including the Luzon Sea and the waters around, within and adjacent to the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc.

articles.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy
articles.summary: According to a complaint filed in federal court in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang

blocks.text: JENSEN HUANG. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang gives a keynote address at CES 2025, an annual consumer electronics trade show, in Las Vegas, Nevada, US, on January 6, 2025.
Steve Marcus/Reuters
According to a complaint filed in federal court in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang
Nvidia and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued on Monday, November 9, in a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang’s ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

According to a complaint filed in federal court in San Jose, California, the defendants misled shareholders about Huang’s alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed who is not related to him, and did not disclose that the matter raised national security concerns that threatened Nvidia’s reputation and business prospects.
The New York Times reported last month about the alleged relationship, and that US authorities had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset.

blocks.caption: Nvidia probes whether CEO Huang was target of foreign intelligence effort as he admits affair

blocks.text: Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Jensen Huang told Nvidia’s employees he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the alleged relationship.

He co-founded Nvidia, and has led the Santa Clara, California-based company as it became the world’s most valuable chipmaker and made him one of the world’s most prominent symbols of the artificial intelligence boom.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on Sunday. Its shares closed down 4.3% on Monday, reducing Nvidia’s market capitalization by approximately $190 billion. The lawsuit was filed five minutes after the US stock market closed.
It is common for shareholders to sue companies after unexpected share price declines. Nvidia shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from the defendants. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Impeachment court warns contempt, perjury cases vs lying witnesses
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero reminded Tuesday that witnesses who lie under oath may be cited in contempt and face perjury charges.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 11:14am
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero reminded Tuesday that witnesses who lie under oath may be cited in contempt and face perjury charges.

Escudero said this on Day 41 of the impeachment trial after Senator-Judge Vicente “Tito” Sotto III asked to be reminded of the penalties and sanctions against those who lie before the impeachment court.
“They may be subject to contempt by the court, your Honor,” the presiding officer said.

“In addition to that, may be subjected to cases of perjury, should one be filed against him before the proper prosecutor’s office and/or courts of law because the statements given by any witness is under oath and is therefore covered by our laws on perjury as well,” he added.
This was echoed by Senator-Judge Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, citing Rule V of Resolution No. 39 on containing the rules of procedure on impeachment trials, which states that:

The Senate shall have power to compel the attendance of witnesses, to enforce obedience to its orders, mandates, writs, and judgments, to preserve order, and to punish in a summary way contempts of, and disobedience to, its authority, orders, mandates, writs, or judgments, and to make all lawful orders, rules, and regulations which it may deem essential or conducive to the ends of justice.

“Yesterday was not a good day for the impeachment court simply because we had a witness who smirked, who laughed, and almost made a mockery of the impeachment trial. And we don’t want to have a repeat of that kind of testimony,” Lacson said.
“Just a reminder to everyone that this is not an implied power of the impeachment court but an expressed power granted by such resolution,” he added.
On Monday, Davao City assessor Engineer Jaime Adalin, the first witness presented by the defense, was grilled by the prosecution and some senator-judges about his travel to China.

During his cross-examination, Adalin said he could not remember details of the trip, but he later admitted traveling to China in January 2026 for “personal” purposes, when he was being questioned by senator-judges.
The witness also said he would submit official documents regarding the trip.
No submission
But Escudero announced Tuesday that Adalin has yet to submit relevant details regarding his trip to China, as requested by Senator-Judge Raffy Tulfo.

The impeachment court presiding officer thus directed the clerk of court to follow up with Adalin regarding the matter, and also remind him to provide the list of properties owned or are in the name of the Vice President and her husband, Atty. Manases Carpio.
“If by tomorrow the same is not yet complied with, unless sufficient cause or reason is given, the court will be forced to issue compulsory process on the same,” Escudero said. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: California voters fail to pass proposed one-time tax on billionaires’ wealth
articles.summary:
Campaign over Prop 40, as measure was known, was most expensive in state history, flush with Silicon Valley dollars

California billionaires won a contentious ballot measure campaign,…

blocks.text: California billionaires won a contentious ballot measure campaign, defeating a proposed one-time tax on their wealth.

The bruising campaign over Proposition 40 was the most expensive in state history and witness to back-and-forth dealing from tech billionaires and democratic leaders, including Gavin Newsom, the governor, who steadfastly opposed the measure. While supporters of Prop 40 cast it as a solution to drastic healthcare cuts from Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill Act, opponents led by prosperous billionaires mounted an influential campaign saying the billionaire tax was instead “an everyone tax”.
This result could hamper nationwide momentum on demands that billionaires pay their fair share and states enacting new laws to tax the ultra-wealthy.

Prop 40 proposed a one-time 5% tax on all individuals in California with a net worth of more than $1bn as of 1 January 2026. It was sponsored by the healthcare union SEIU-United Healthcare Workers West, and dictated that the proceeds from the tax would fund healthcare programs, along with some education and food assistance.

The state’s major unions, and progressive politicians such as Bernie Sanders, the Vermont senator, and Ro Khanna, a California congressman, backed Prop 40. But both the Democratic and Republican candidates for governor, as well as organizations such as Planned Parenthood Affiliates of California, a lobbying branch of the healthcare group, opposed it – pointing to its structure as a one-off tax that would only fund certain healthcare programs. Prop 40’s most vocal critics, however, were the state’s billionaires.

Donors to the opposition campaign were a who’s who of Silicon Valley, including executives from Google, Palantir, DoorDash, Stripe and Reddit, along with several prominent venture capitalists. The biggest donor, by far, was Sergey Brin, a Google co-founder, who contributed at least $132m to fight the tax, according to campaign finance filings.

All told, the billionaires mounted a nearly $425m battle against Prop 40, making it the most expensive opposition campaign in state history. In the first two weeks of October, spending surpassed $2.5m a day, according to the most recent campaign finance filings.

Part of the opposition campaign’s strategy was mounting two separate counter-measures on the ballot, Proposition 41 and 42. Prop 41 directly targeted the billionaire tax, while Prop 42 was a general proposal on limiting certain new taxes and would ban any taxation on billionaire wealth. If either measure received more yes votes than Prop 40, they would stop the billionaire tax from taking effect – even if it passed.
Supporters of the billionaire tax called Props 41 and 42 “poison pills”.

articles.title: Trump says Iran war is 'effectively over' militarily with further strikes unlikely
articles.summary: The president says the US is keeping "status quo" with Iran but remains “locked and loaded” should the situation in the Middle East change.

blocks.text: Donald Trump says the Iran war "militarily is effectively over" declaring that there is "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the Middle East conflict.
"We're just keeping it the status quo," the US president said on Monday. "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."

Addressing reporters from the White House press briefing room, Trump said that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely" but that the US was "locked and loaded" should the circumstances change.
Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubts about the US president's prior comments about resolving the conflict.
Responding to a question over why he would not officially declare an end to the conflict, Trump said that some of the Gulf allies could still face Iranian aggression.
"We have some great allies there and we have to make sure they're not hurt," Trump said, suggesting that the US naval blockade on Iranian ports was helping to make the region more secure.
Trump hosted Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdul Rahman Al Thani in the Oval Office earlier on Monday, saying they had an "excellent conversation" about negotiations to end the war.
In a post on X, the Qatari prime minister said he held "positive discussions" with Trump and Vice-President JD Vance on "reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region".
Efforts to broker a peace between Washington and Tehran have largely been held indirectly through mediators since the war first broke out following joint US-Israeli strikes in February.

Saudi Arabia, Qatar and United Arab Emirates are among the US's Gulf allies that have been hit by Iranian strikes over the course of the war, in addition to threat of strikes that have led to major air travel disruptions in the region.
This is not the first time that Trump has said Iran war is "militarily" over, but the circumstances for him are different now.
Trump has hinted at de-escalation in Iran after a bruising set of midterm election results for the Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President Vance blamed on the Iran War.
In an interview with 60 minutes that aired on Sunday, the president said he did not currently see "any reason" to escalate the war.
Ahead of the midterms, Trump said US forces conducted what he described as "minor strikes" on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Post-election recriminations over the US war in Iran are already placing pressure on members of the Trump administration.

Republican congressman Thomas Massie launched a strong attack against Trump's Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday over the war in Iran, requesting a vote in the House of Representatives to impeach him.
Trump has backed Hegseth, who says he is "not worried" about the looming impeachment threats, calling Massie's effort a "sham".

While the move is unlikely to succeed with Republicans still in control of Congress until January, Democrats have expressed willingness to impeach Hegseth once the new session begins and they have control of both the House and the Senate.

articles.title: Australia to introduce mandatory reporting after OpenAI hack to combat artificial intelligence ‘going rogue’
articles.summary:
Government flags criminal law changes to ensure companies can’t argue in future ‘that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded’

OpenAI won’t face criminal penalties over the Medicare hack…

blocks.text: OpenAI won’t face criminal penalties over the Medicare hack but the prime minister has flagged changes to Australia’s criminal law to crack down on future breaches by artificial intelligence companies.
Anthony Albanese on Tuesday released the recommendations of a “rapid review” into the June breach but not the findings or the report itself.

A key recommendation is for the attorney general’s department, the Australian federal police and home affairs to consider reforming the law to introduce “penalties for egregious regulatory non-compliance” and a “failure to prevent” offence which would criminalise developing an AI model that engaged in harmful conduct while failing “to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm”.
The review recommended the federal government “consider mandatory, time-bound AI safety reporting, including but not limited to misaligned behaviour or agentic cyber incidents”.

The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, told reporters “we need to make sure that our laws and our systems keep pace with the technology and also make sure that we’re able to use the technology to find vulnerabilities before others do”.

“The mandatory reporting, when artificial intelligence goes rogue, gives us a chance to be able to make sure that when this happens, the reporting occurs and occurs immediately,” Burke said in Canberra alongside the PM.
On the “concept of looking at how we can update our criminal law”, Burke said: “It should never be the case that there’s an argument that someone didn’t know the computer was loaded.”
“We need to make sure that the criminal law is up to date for how this new technology is able to act.”
Albanese on Tuesday characterised OpenAI’s breach of Services Australia as “minor” in terms of the implications for personal privacy.
“The clear indication is that no information was got that involves people’s personal details,” the prime minister told reporters in Canberra.
“All of that was confirmed essentially ... but that doesn’t mean that it wasn’t a serious issue and that in other areas there might be more serious implications.”
The review made 18 recommendations. Albanese said “we accept all of the recommendations and we’ve commenced work to implement them”.
Albanese did not directly answer a question about whether the OpenAI incident in June would have breached the proposed new laws if they were in place.
The AI agent developed by OpenAI accessed Services Australia data and three other systems in June.
The company didn’t notify the Australia government until mid-September despite becoming aware of the incident itself in August.
Guardian Australia revealed last month OpenAI used AI to help write the email to notify Australian authorities.
Albanese said the government would set up a new AI safety regulator.
Labor would consider six key obligations on AI companies, including:

items: maintaining security controls across all stages of development and deployment;
identify and manage serious risks associated with their models;
provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian government rapidly;
allow independent evaluation of their models;
maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management, and transparency;
and respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change.

articles.title: Robredo-Tulfo tandem leads Octa's hypothetical matchup for 2028 polls
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo and Sen. Raffy Tulfo led a hypothetical 2028 presidential and vice presidential matchup against Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte and Sen. Robin…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Naga City Mayor Leni Robredo and Sen. Raffy Tulfo led a hypothetical 2028 presidential and vice presidential matchup against Davao City Mayor Baste Duterte and Sen. Robin Padilla, an Octa Research survey showed.
According to the survey, conducted from Sept. 28 to Oct. 4, 43 percent of adult Filipinos said they would vote for the Robredo-Tulfo tandem.
Meanwhile, 39 percent said they would choose the Duterte-Padilla tandem, while 18 percent chose neither tandem or said they did not know.
This is the first time Octa has conducted a survey on the pairing.
“There are no earlier OCTA data on this pairing, so the figures serve as a baseline against which future survey waves can be compared,” it said.

blocks.caption: Table from Octa Research

blocks.text: At least 1,200 adult Filipinos nationwide were surveyed through face-to-face interviews. The survey had a ±3 percent margin of error and a 95 percent confidence level.
The Robredo-Tulfo tandem was ahead by four percentage points, just above the ±3 percent margin of error.
According to Octa, the four-point lead “is slight, and neither tandem commands majority support.”

The Robredo-Tulfo tandem posted its strongest showing in Balance Luzon, with 61 percent against 19 percent for Duterte-Padilla. Support for the tandem reached 69 percent in North Luzon and 53 percent in South Luzon, while 28 percent were uncommitted.
They also led in the National Capital Region, with 49 percent against 32 percent, while 18 percent were uncommitted.
The Duterte-Padilla tandem posted its strongest showing in Mindanao, where it received 81 percent support, compared with only 4 percent for the Robredo-Tulfo pairing.

blocks.caption: Davao City Mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte and Sen. Robin Padilla

blocks.text: The two tandems were closely divided in the Visayas, with 43 percent supporting Duterte-Padilla and 41 percent backing Robredo-Tulfo.
By socioeconomic class, about four in five adults in Class D were evenly split between the two pairs, with each receiving 41 percent.

“The Robredo–Tulfo tandem leads in the smaller Classes ABC and E, and within Class D the two tandems split along the D1 and D2 segments, but these gaps are modest compared with the regional and ethnolinguistic ones,” it explained.
Octa noted that the results remained a “snapshot and baseline” and were likely to change, particularly because the Davao City mayor had not yet declared a presidential bid.
Meanwhile, Robredo reiterated on Monday that she would not seek any national post in the May 2028 elections.

“With the lead slight, the uncommitted bloc large, and the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte still unresolved, this matchup remains an early and open baseline — not a prediction of the May 2028 outcome,” Octa said. /mcm

articles.title: Disconnected dikes, sloppy plans: Why millions in flood control projects failed Bulakan
articles.summary: In some areas, residents had to raise the ground around their properties with fill soil — just so the flood control structures can work as intended

blocks.text: BULACAN, Philippines – For more than a week in August, following days of successive typhoons, floodwaters submerged parts of Triple Junction Subdivision in Barangay Matungao, Bulakan town in this province, giving residents no choice but to use boats to get around.

Nico (not his real name) said it was the worst flooding he had experienced in Triple Junction. “Nung mga nakaraang taon, normal naman na nakakaranas kami ng baha. Pero itong lately, this 2025, tapos nung taon na ‘to, grabe ‘yung baha kasi ultimo konting ulan lang, mahinang bagyo, lumalalim agad ‘yung tubig,” he added. (“In previous years, flooding was normal for us. But lately, in 2025 and this year, the floods have been severe. Even with just a little rain or a weak storm, the water rises quickly.”)
All this despite millions of taxpayers’ money spent on flood control structures in the town.

From 2022 to 2024, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) 1st District Engineering Office recorded 12 completed flood control projects in Bulakan, with a combined contract cost of P722.8 million. These included riverbank reinforcements, revetments, and concrete structures built along waterways. (READ: What’s a flood control project, anyway?)

However, residents and barangay officials continue to report unfinished sections of flood control structures. The gap between the recorded project status and conditions described on the ground raises questions about their implementation and effectiveness.
Four of the projects are located in Matungao, including structures along the Guiguinto River near Triple Junction.

Fernando Siringan of the University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute explained in a series of social media posts that the coastal plains of Bulacan, Pampanga, and Camanava (Caloocan, Malabon, Navotas, Valenzuela — all in Metro Manila) were formed over thousands of years by sediments carried downstream by rivers. Much of the area sits only 0 to 2 meters above sea level, leaving little difference in elevation to help water drain naturally toward the sea.
High tides make the problem worse. When sea levels rise, river water drains more slowly into Manila Bay, allowing water to back up and remain in low-lying communities.

Siringan also identified human activities that can worsen flooding. “Channels have narrowed due to structural encroachments, including residential housing, fishponds, reclaimed banks, river walls, and protruding bridge abutments. Simultaneously, severe upstream soil erosion and urban garbage accumulate on riverbeds,” he stated in a September 10 post.

For Bulakan, this means flood-control structures along individual riverbanks are only part of the equation. The municipality also has to contend with the condition of its rivers, drainage networks, and the routes through which water enters and leaves the area.

Barangay captain Anthony Mark R. Cruz said that some flood control structures in Matungao remain unfinished, with the sections of dikes “disconnected” from one another. They end up being useless, because the structures get in the way when water begins to recede, he said in Filipino.

The projects did not seem to have taken into account how water moves through nearby communities. In some areas, residents had to raise the ground around their properties with fill soil — just so the flood-control structures can work as intended.

blocks.caption: 5 DPWH Bulacan engineers suspended over P118-M anomalous flood control projects

blocks.text: “Dito kasi sa looban, hindi rin kasi magiging lebel ‘yung cuffing ng flood control, hindi rin magiging lebel ng lupa, so possible talaga, kailangan, magtambak din talaga sila resident para lang mapakinabangan ‘yung flood control.” (“In the inner parts of the barangay, the flood control structure will not be level with the ground. Residents may actually need to raise the elevation of their properties with fill soil just to benefit from the flood control project.”)

Cruz said barangay officials need to be consulted before construction begins; they know which areas could be affected. But their involvement in monitoring projects remains limited, leaving them with little opportunity to verify whether completed structures follow approved plans or account for conditions on the ground.

blocks.caption: WHERE TAXES GO. The P77-million flood wall project at Triple Junction subdivision in Bulakan town.

blocks.text: Sometimes, he said, they would find out that a project has been completed after the workers had already left the site. It would be better if barangay inspections are made before a project is declared finished.
Matungao is also burdened by a poor drainage system.

Cruz said some channels lack functioning outlets, including the closed drainage outfall in Purok 2. Other drainage lines have been blocked, particularly those passing through two private subdivisions in the barangay.
With the barangay unable to finance a comprehensive drainage system on its own, Cruz said local officials would have to seek funding from the national government.

Matungao’s National Tax Allotment (NTA) increased from P13.9 million in 2024 to P19.6 million in 2026, with an indicative allocation of P21.7 million for 2027. Of the barangay’s 2026 NTA, only around 1% is allocated for infrastructure, amounting to approximately P200,000 to P250,000 annually. Of this amount, a measly P150,000 is earmarked for drainage projects.

“It’s difficult. We want to help everyone, but our budget is simply not sufficient for that,” he said in Filipino. “We can only do what the barangay can afford and make do with whatever funding the municipality provides.”

blocks.caption: CLOGGED. Drainage works alongside Matungao Street in Bulakan town.

blocks.text: Triple Junction was privately owned before it was turned over to the local government in 2000, during the establishment of the Bulacan State University (BulSU) Meneses campus. Its location beside the Guiguinto River has long exposed residents to flooding from the river.

Rosalyn, a Triple Junction homeowners association (HOA) member who requested anonymity, said road-raising works should be preceded by drainage improvements. Some residents have raised their homes to match the elevated roads, but she said this has not been enough to address flooding.

“Even the BulSU covered court can no longer be used,” she said in Filipino. “The surrounding area is also flooded. Look at the water levels now: they rise whether it is low tide or high tide. The people living there are the ones who suffer.”

Rosalyn pointed to gaps in the dike built as flood control inside Triple Junction, whose uneven construction leaves some sections higher than others, with several portions still open. These openings allow high-tide waters to enter the subdivision. When water also drains out slowly, it takes longer for flood levels to recede.

Water entering Triple Junction from neighboring towns of Balagtas and Guiguinto points to the need for coordination among municipalities, particularly when road-raising and drainage projects can redirect water across jurisdictional boundaries. Rosalyn urged local governments to agree on where excess water should flow before undertaking such projects.

Drainage routes through private subdivisions also require coordination with property owners to keep waterways unobstructed, Cruz noted. Rosalyn and Cruz both identified river dredging as a necessary measure to improve water flow.

“Floodwalls are not enough,” Rosalyn said. “They are not sufficient. Water still gets in. No matter how many dikes you build, if the river itself is not properly maintained, the first thing that needs to be done is to dredge it,” she added.

However, after living in Triple Junction for 23 years, Nico said he didn’t think dredging has helped. He said the excavation may have worsened flooding in Matungao, which he described as a natural catch basin for floodwaters. “Since they excavated the river here, it seems like the elevation of our area has gone even lower. It doesn’t seem to have helped,” he said in Filipino.

The differing views on dredging underscore the need for flood control measures to account for entire waterways and the communities they affect. While government planning and coordination are essential, residents also have a role in reducing flood risks.

Rosalyn shared that they have taken steps to reduce risks by reminding residents to follow garbage collection schedules, segregate waste, and put out trash only when collection trucks are due. The HOA also encouraged the homeowners to cut down on single-use plastics.

Nico’s family, on other hand, follows the HOA’s waste-management measures as its own contribution to preventing floods. He also called for greater community awareness of proper waste segregation and disaster preparedness, urging the local government to conduct seminars for residents who may lack the knowledge to properly manage their waste or prepare for calamities.
But he stressed that these efforts, no matter how consistent, cannot address the community’s larger problems without responsive leadership.

Under Department Order No. 23, series of 2015, the DPWH requires flood control and drainage projects to be based on a master plan or feasibility study for the river basin or urban area they cover. Engineering surveys must identify technical issues and possible alternatives, while project effectiveness is measured by reductions in flood-prone areas, property damage, and the duration of flooding.

DPWH records list 12 flood control projects as completed in Bulakan from 2022 to 2024. Yet residents’ accounts of unfinished structures, obstructed drainage, and prolonged flooding raise questions about how these projects fit into the municipality’s wider drainage and flood-control network.

Addressing these problems also requires coordination beyond Bulakan. Infrastructure projects in neighboring municipalities can affect how water moves across boundaries, while drainage routes passing through private subdivisions require cooperation with property owners. (As of writing, the DPWH 1st District Engineering Office had yet to respond to queries about the flood control projects in Bulakan.)

Residents can help manage waste and prepare for emergencies, but these efforts cannot repair obstructed drainage or compensate for unfinished infrastructure. Bulakan needs more than additional flood control structures. It needs a coordinated plan based on the municipality’s terrain, waterways, drainage systems, and connections to neighboring communities.
For those who continue to wait days for floodwaters to recede, that plan cannot come too late.

“Under our current system, we do not know what plans the government has for us,” Cruz said in Filipino. “Sometimes, they should also look at what is happening on the ground. We are often the ones blamed. Yes, this is our job, and we have sworn to fulfill this duty, but the government has its responsibilities, too. I hope we can work together.” – Rappler.com

Mark David Silencio is an information technology student at the Bulacan State University in Plaridel, Bulacan. An Aries Rufo Journalism Fellow for 2026, he is also the managing editor for Administration of Pacesetter.

articles.title: Police investigate as nearly 30 Santa Barbara half-marathon runners fall ill with ‘unusual symptoms’
articles.summary:
Runners seek medical treatment as 13-mile race held amid unusually high November temperatures

Police in southern California are investigating the circumstances that led to the…

blocks.text: Police in southern California are investigating the circumstances that led to the hospitalization of nearly 30 runners who participated in the Santa Barbara Half on Sunday.

Santa Barbara police said in a statement to the Associated Press that they had opened an investigation after receiving reports from Santa Barbara Cottage Hospital about multiple half-marathon participants seeking medical treatment for “unusual symptoms”.
Cottage Health said in a statement it had a “larger than expected number of emergency visits … a number of them with similar symptoms of undetermined cause”.
Race organizers say they believe any illness is attributable to heat or dehydration. The high on the day of the race was 88F (31.1C), an unusually high temperature for this time of year.

Neither the hospital nor police have detailed the symptoms beyond calling them unusual. Cottage Health said on Monday that 27 participants came to emergency rooms in Santa Barbara and Goleta, a small city about 10 miles west.
More than 4,640 people competed in the half-marathon, which spanned about 13 miles, according to the Santa Barbara Half Marathon website.

Of those who were either taken to the hospital or arrived there on their own, 24 patients had been treated and discharged as of Monday morning. The three others were in stable condition, the company told the Associated Press.

Event director David Monico said organizers transported 15 people from the medical tent to local hospitals. He said the event’s medical team treated numerous runners for dehydration and overheating both on the course and at the finish line.

The half-marathon’s event director, David Monico told the Guardian that they have “no additional information to suggest that the issues some of the participants experienced were caused by anything other than endurance event exertion-related symptoms”.

articles.title: Senators urge state of calamity declaration in El Niño-hit areas
articles.summary: Twenty senators have signed a resolution calling on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare a state of calamity in areas affected by the strong El Niño phenomenon.

blocks.text: Published November 10, 2026 10:15am
Twenty senators have signed a resolution calling on President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. to declare a state of calamity in areas affected by the strong El Niño phenomenon.

Under proposed Senate Resolution 765, the President is urged, upon the recommendation of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC), to declare a state of calamity under Republic Act (RA) 10121, or the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act, in areas experiencing drought-related disaster impacts.

The President may also declare a state of imminent disaster as warranted under RA 12287, or the Declaration of State of Imminent Disaster Act, in areas facing “highly probable disasters with projected catastrophic impacts,” as determined through appropriate disaster risk assessment.

The resolution was signed by Senate Agriculture, Food and Agrarian Reform committee chairperson Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, as well as Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian and Senators Vicente Sotto III, Juan Miguel Zubiri, Alan Peter Cayetano, Imee Marcos, Robin Padilla, Bam Aquino, Risa Hontiveros, JV Ejercito, Lito Lapid, Joel Villanueva, Erwin Tulfo, Raffy Tulfo, Ping Lacson, Chiz Escudero, Pia Cayetano, Bong Go, Camille Villar, and Mark Villar.

The senators also urged the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) and concerned agencies to mobilize available and eligible funds under the 2026 national budget, including the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund and agency Quick Response Funds.

They also called on concerned agencies and local price coordination councils to monitor the prices of basic necessities and prime commodities, and to take action against overpricing, profiteering, and hoarding in affected areas.
As of October 21, the agricultural sector incurred P8.57 billion in damage and losses due to El Niño, according to the Department of Agriculture (DA).

The agricultural damage was reportedly recorded in Cordillera Administrative Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, CALABARZON, MIMAROPA, Bicol Region, Western Visayas, Negros Island Region, Central Visayas, Eastern Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Davao Region, SOCCSKSARGEN, and Caraga.
The DA earlier proposed a P61.99-billion action plan to mitigate the impact of El Niño on the country’s food supply and livelihoods.
The proposed spending package includes P6.2 billion already released under the government’s Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Program. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: Marcos gov’t on track to miss growth target for fourth straight year
articles.summary: Even achieving 3% growth in 2026 would be a 'remarkable accomplishment,' says economic planning chief Arsenio Balisacan

blocks.text: TWO WORLDS. Informal settlements stand in contrast to Manila's modern high-rise buildings on July 9, 2026.
Rappler
Even achieving 3% growth in 2026 would be a 'remarkable accomplishment,' says economic planning chief Arsenio Balisacan

items: The Philippine economy is experiencing its weakest growth since 2009, with GDP growing only 2.1% in Q3 2026, falling short of expectations and lagging behind regional neighbors.
The government has revised its full-year growth target down to 3.5% to 4.5%, but achieving even this lower target seems unlikely without a significant fourth-quarter rebound.
Despite challenges, there are signs of cautious optimism with exports growing by 8.6%, and the government plans to reassess growth forecasts in December.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s administration is staring at yet another year of missed economic growth targets, with the Philippine economy slowing for a fifth consecutive quarter and sinking to its weakest pace since 2009, outside the pandemic.

The latest gross domestic product (GDP) figures showed the economy growing by just 2.1% in Q3 2026 from 2.4% in the previous quarter and 4% a year earlier, a surprisingly weak performance when most economists had expected a modest rebound.

The Philippines has also once again lagged well behind its Southeast Asian neighbors. Vietnam’s economy surged by 9.95% in the third quarter, while Indonesia grew by 5.47%. Even the more mature economies of Singapore and Malaysia expanded by 5.4% and 5.3%, respectively, according to their governments’ preliminary estimates. Elsewhere, Taiwan raced ahead, growing 14.36% due to booming demand for artificial intelligence and semiconductors.

Closer to home, it’s been a rough year for the local economy. After a disappointing first half, Marcos’ economic managers had already slashed their full-year growth target from 5% to 6% to just 3.5% to 4.5%. Now, even that lower target is looking out of reach.

With GDP growing by just 2.5% throughout 2026 so far, the economy would need to post a monumentally strong fourth-quarter growth of about 6.3% to reach even the lower end of its already reduced annual target of 3.5% to 4.5%.
Department of Economy, Planning, and Development Secretary Arsenio Balisacan was hardly optimistic.
“It’s very, very challenging at this point given the current environment,” Balisacan told reporters.
He said even achieving full-year growth of 3% would already be a “remarkable achievement,” requiring the economy to grow by around 4% to 4.5% in the fourth quarter.
But even such an outcome would extend the Marcos administration’s record of missing its annual economic growth targets.

In 2023, GDP grew by only 5.5%, below the government’s 6% to 7% target. Growth reached 5.7% in 2024, again missing the revised 6% to 6.5% target, before slowing to 4.4% in 2025, missing the target of 5.5% to 6.5%.

Ironically enough, lackluster government spending has itself become part of the problem. Public construction investment contracted by another 15.1% in Q3 2026. Balisacan agreed that the flood control corruption scandal had made government agencies “a bit cautious” about continuing with infrastructure projects, particularly those already underway.

blocks.caption: From ghost projects to growth slump, Marcos now faces a spending dilemma

blocks.text: There are, however, some reasons for cautious optimism. Exports grew by 8.6%, supported by stronger demand for electronics and AI-related products. Overall investments also contracted less at 0.2%.

The country’s chief economist was also more upbeat about recovery next year, saying that attaining 5% to 6% growth “remains possible, but requires stronger investment, easing price pressure, and renewed confidence.”
The government’s economic managers are set to meet in early December to revisit their growth forecasts and targets, including the projected 5% to 6% expansion in 2027. – Rappler.com

articles.title: China rocket causes 'space jellyfish' over Palawan, WPS
articles.summary: The launch of a Chinese rocket caused a "space jellyfish" to appear over Puerto Princesa City and several islands in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) on Monday, the Philippine Navy said.

blocks.text: PH NAVY SAYS
Published November 10, 2026 10:07am
The launch of a Chinese rocket caused a "space jellyfish" to appear over Puerto Princesa City and several islands in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) on Monday, the Philippine Navy said.
In a statement, the Naval Command West (NCW) said all its units and assets were placed on heightened alert as part of its precautionary measures.

"All Philippine Navy units and assets under the Command were placed on heightened alert status to ensure operational readiness and facilitate the immediate reporting and assessment of any potential incidents within the Command's area of operations," the NCW said.
China's Long March-12 rocket was launched from the Hainan International Commercial Launch Center in Wenchang, Hainan at 4:24 a.m. on Monday, according to the Command.

At 4:33 a.m., personnel in Puerto Princesa City observed a bright, cone-shaped, and luminous vapor trail moving from the northwest toward the southeast, accompanied by a bright red-orange streak of light.
The phenomenon, which remained visible for around one minute and 29 seconds, is commonly referred to as a "space jellyfish."
At around 4:37 a.m., observers also reported hearing a loud explosive sound, followed by two lower-intensity sounds at around 4:38 a.m. and subsequent rumbling.
The Navy said these sounds were assessed to be potentially linked to the rocket's ascent and atmospheric flight.
Similar sightings were reported by personnel stationed in several Philippine-held islands in the WPS.
At Lawak and Patag Stations, personnel spotted white luminous trails approximately 60 to 70 nautical miles east of their respective locations.
At Likas Station, a faint white light was seen about 100 nautical miles northeast.

At Rizal Reef Station, personnel spotted a white luminous trail approximately 80 nautical miles east-southeast of the station. The object was estimated to be 4,500 to 5,500 feet above sea level and was seen moving southeast before disappearing.
At Tubbataha Station, meanwhile, personnel observed a bright luminous object approximately 19 nautical miles from their location.
The NCW said the space jellyfish phenomenon "was likely caused by the expansion of rocket exhaust gases at high altitude, illuminated by sunlight while observers on the ground remained in darkness."
"Such visual effects are commonly associated with rocket launches conducted during pre-dawn or twilight conditions."
The Command said it was maintaining coordination with partner government agencies, coastal communities, and local fisherfolk to strengthen information-sharing.
This is to ensure the timely reporting of suspected rocket debris, falling objects, and other related maritime and aerial incidents.
"The Naval Command West emphasizes the importance of sustained vigilance amid developments involving rocket launch activities in the region," the NCW said.

"The Command remains steadfast in safeguarding the country's maritime interests and ensuring the safety of communities and personnel through inter-agency cooperation, continuous monitoring, and a proactive maritime security posture," it added. —VAL, GMA News
